newsitem.title: USA: Harcourt to acquire National Education.
newsitem.headline: Harcourt to acquire National Education.

text.p: Publisher Harcourt General Inc. said Tuesday it agreed to buy National Education Corp. for about $800 million, topping its previous $740 million offer.

The agreement breaks up a merger agreement between National Education and Sylvan Learning Systems Inc. Harcourt said Sylvan, which had agreed on a stock swap with National Education that was originally worth $750 million, would receive a $30 million payment.

Harcourt said it would pay $21 a share in cash for National Education, up from its initial offer of $19.50 a share. It said the offer, which originally was worth about $777 million, included additional National Education stock options.
National Education's stock added 37.5 cents to $20.875 in early trading Tuesday, and Harcourt fell 50 cents to $46.625, both on the New York Stock Exchange. Sylvan rose $2 to $34.875 on Nasdaq.
Harcourt said the Hart-Scott-Rodino anti-trust waiting period for the tender offer had expired. "Consummation of the merger is subject to customary terms and conditions," it said.

A Harcourt official said the company would advance $30 million to National Education to enable it to make the payment to Sylvan. Harcourt would be entitled to a reimbursement from National Education if the merger should not be completed, he said.

Harcourt launched its rival bid for National Education in April after Sylvan offered 0.58 share of its own stock for each National Education share in an offer originally valued at $750 million. However, Sylvan's offer ended up being worth about $670 million, less than Harcourt's.
Based in Chestnut Hill, Harcourt is a publishing and speciality retailing company. Its revenues in fiscal 1996 were $3.29 billion.

Irvine, Calif.-based National Education, whose operations include ICS Learning Systems, National Education Training Group and Steck-Vaughn Publishing Corporation, had revenues of $288.8 million in 1996.
